chunks: And with this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn ʿUrwah, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurārah, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
Concerning a man who forgets to wipe his head until he enters into the salat (prayer),
He عليه السلام said: "If there is moisture in his beard enough for him to wipe his head and his feet, then let him do that and let him pray."
He عليه السلام said: "And if he forgets anything from the obligatory wudu (ablution), then he must begin with what he forgot and repeat what remains for the completion of the wudu (ablution)."

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the salat (prayer) into which he has entered
key_terms.الْمَفْرُوضِ: that which is obligatory and prescribed
key_terms.الْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)
key_terms.بَلَلٌ: moisture or wetness remaining for ritual wiping
key_terms.رَأْسِهِ: his head, the part to be wiped in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.لِحْيَتِهِ: his beard, from which remaining moisture may be used
key_terms.مَسْحَ: wiping as part of the prescribed acts of wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يُعِيدَ: he repeats the remaining acts to complete the proper order

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he forgets to wipe his head in wudu (ablution) until after entering the salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling for one who forgets part of the obligatory wudu (ablution), specifically wiping the head, and only remembers after entering the salat (prayer). It states that if sufficient moisture remains in the beard, he may use it to complete the wiping; more generally, if an obligatory part of wudu (ablution) was omitted, he must resume from the forgotten part and redo the remaining sequence to complete the wudu (ablution) properly.
